title: Aging and protocol dependence of thermal activation events in structural glasses
abstract: In this study, we investigate the waiting time dependence and the protocol dependence of thermally activated events in structural glasses using molecular simulations and potential energy landscape analysis. We find a qualitative crossover in the nature of activation events; from avalanche-like events to local events. We also use the isoconfigurational ensemble analysis and reveal that the events become less diverse and more reversible. We discuss these crossovers from the perspective of the stability and the potential energy landscape of glasses. To investigate the protocol dependence, we compare the two types of glasses whose stability is controlled by waiting time and parent temperature, respectively. Surprisingly, at the same inherent structure energy level, the parent-temperature-controlled glasses are more unstable and maintain their avalanche-like nature. These results demonstrate that the activation properties of structural glasses are not determined solely by their energy levels, highlighting the essential role of state connectivity and the dynamical sampling in the complex energy landscape.
summary: This work investigates how thermal activation events occur in structural glasses by analyzing their dependence on waiting time and preparation protocol. Using molecular simulations, the authors find a crossover in event character and demonstrate that the system's stability is governed by more than just its energy level. This highlights the crucial role of state connectivity and dynamical sampling in determining glass behavior.
main_problem: The study investigates the waiting time dependence and protocol dependence of thermally activated events in structural glasses.
main_result: Activation properties are not solely determined by energy levels, as the parent-temperature-controlled glasses were found to be more unstable and maintain an avalanche-like nature compared to waiting-time-controlled ones.
method: The research employs molecular simulations using Langevin dynamics, potential energy landscape analysis, and isoconfigurational ensemble analysis.
model_or_system: The system models structural glasses using the modified Kob-Andersen model in two dimensions (a binary mixture). Dynamics are simulated using underdamped Langevin dynamics.
key_observables: Waiting time dependence of potential energy, nature of activation events (avalanche-like vs. local), effective number of paths, and reversibility.
important_parameters: Waiting time ($t_w$), parent temperature, and the inherent structure energy level ($e_{IS}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing different control protocols (waiting time vs. parent temperature) to probe the underlying energy landscape structure.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the logarithmic or weak power-law decrease of $e_{IS}$ with waiting time, and the analysis tracks the crossover in event nature.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the waiting time dependence, observing a crossover from avalanche-like to local events, and then contrasts the results obtained from waiting-time-controlled versus parent-temperature-controlled glasses to highlight the role of state connectivity.
why_interesting: The findings regarding the failure of energy-level arguments to predict dynamics are highly relevant to understanding complex energy landscapes in disordered systems, which share conceptual links with many-body dynamics in amorphous materials.
